message: Just to be sure I have the income right: did you mean about $55,000 to $75,000 a year? The $550,000 to $750,000 figure would be far higher than most families earn. Also, I didn't get an answer on the children's ages: is any child under 5, and is anyone pregnant or is there a baby under 1?
reply: Somewhere between 550 thousand and 750 thousand a year. Hard to say. I don't really know.

summary: Based on what you told me (Hawaii, household of 4 with 2 children under 18, all in their thirties and healthy, household earnings of about $550,000 to $750,000 a year), I don't recommend applying for any of the ten programmes. At that income, the household is above the limits for SNAP, WIC, TANF, SSI, Medicaid, CHIP, EITC, the refundable child tax credit, the ACA premium tax credit, and free or reduced-price school meals. The child tax credit also phases out completely at this income. You said you're not sure of the income figure, so I'm handing this to a caseworker to confirm it. If the household's actual yearly income is much lower (for example, around $55,000 to $75,000), please tell us, and we can re-screen, since several programmes (possibly WIC, CHIP, school meals, the child tax credit, and the ACA premium tax credit) could then apply.
